evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Colonies, relocation and losses
evidence.text: “Losing ships” are encounter participants that should suffer defeat's loss; ships “lost to warp” actually reach it involuntarily at some point in the encounter. “Sent” ships reach the warp through a specific action or effect, sometimes voluntarily, while not directly involved in the encounter; they count as lost rather than encounter-losing ships. An interruption preventing warp arrival means no actual warp loss. These distinctions matter for compensation, Healer, Observer, Void and Zombie.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Zombie
evidence.text:
- Whenever own ships should be lost to warp, instead return them to any own colonies and keep using them.
- May free ANY player's ships from warp back to any colonies that player has as part of deal.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Vacuum
evidence.text: **FAQ pp2,15,21–22:** Never target yourself. Your actual warp loss triggers before Healer retrieves your ships. Under Vacuum Super, losses from a single effect occur simultaneously: Zombie cannot preserve one disappearing one-ship colony by moving its saved ship to another colony being eliminated by that same effect.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Void
evidence.text: **FAQ pp18,21–22:** Void eradicates directly instead of sending to warp, so it overrides Zombie and Observer; those eradicated ships earn no compensation. Ships protected by your minimum-five-surviving-ships limit go to warp normally instead. A failed deal is not a win and does not eradicate its three-ship penalty.

evidence.heading: Kamikaze
evidence.quote:
#### Kamikaze

**Sacrifice — Main player only; optional; Planning.**

- Before encounter cards selected may send up to four own ships from any own colonies to warp. Draw two deck cards for every ship sent.
- If power zapped, sacrificed ships are not lost to warp.

**FAQ p16:** Choose and sacrifice all ships for a use together before drawing, rather than one at a time while inspecting draws. Play Kamikaze Super anew each encounter in which its effect is wanted.

evidence.heading: Warpish
evidence.quote:
#### Warpish

**Necromancy — Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.**

- After revealing attack add 1 to own total for EACH ship in warp, yours or otherwise.

**FAQ p22:** Count warp ships at your power's use. Ships arriving before it count; later arrivals do not retroactively increase its bonus. Use normal timing for simultaneous effects.

evidence.text: Ships landing on colonies do so simultaneously, including ships released by Mobius Tubes (FAQ p19, general landing rule). With Mobius Tubes and no colony to receive released ships, return those ships to warp; offense may first place up to four of its released ships in the gate.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Zombie
evidence.text:
- Whenever own ships should be lost to warp, instead return them to any own colonies and keep using them.
- May free ANY player's ships from warp back to any colonies that player has as part of deal.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 3. Launch
evidence.text: The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 1. Regroup
evidence.text: Offense must retrieve one of its ships from the warp if available, placing it on any existing home or foreign colony. The original rulebook puts this retrieved ship directly in the gate if offense has no colonies. The FAQ adds that a player who has no colonies or ships on their turn may instead place the Regroup ship on any home planet. Ordinary relocation with no colony to receive ships sends them to the warp; the stated Regroup exceptions take precedence.

evidence.heading: Masochist
evidence.quote:
#### Masochist

**Hurt Yourself — As any player; mandatory; Regroup.**

- At start of any player's regroup phase, BEFORE offense retrieves warp ship, use power to win if all your ships lost.
- Lost ships include those in warp, removed from game, and captured by other players.
- Do not lose power for too few home colonies. May still win normally.

**FAQ p17:** Play Masochist Super anew in each encounter where its effect is wanted.

evidence.heading: Dictator
evidence.quote:
#### Dictator

**Command — Not offense; mandatory; Destiny.**

- When not offense, before destiny chosen, use power to take destiny deck, look through it and choose any card; played as though offense had drawn it.
- On own turn, or any time zapped, remaining destiny cards shuffled and one dealt randomly.

literal_question.question: For Mind Wild, Reserve Wild and Vulch Super, must the flare be replayed for each later qualifying event in that encounter, or does one play last through the encounter? When is Vulch Super first played, and may Vulch collect that same Super through its effect? While Reserve Wild remains active, whose discarded cards of what type may its user take, and where do those cards go? Is each eligible Reserve Wild pickup compulsory or separately optional; if the user declines one, may it still take a later eligible discard? If several otherwise-eligible flares are discarded at the same time while Vulch Super is active, may its power apply to all of them or only one from that group?

required_facts: One play of each listed flare lasts through the current encounter, allowing the eligible later triggering events without replay.
Vulch Super is played the first time eligible flares are discarded in that encounter.
Vulch cannot retrieve its own Super by that effect.
Whenever another player discards a reinforcement card during the remaining encounter, Reserve Wild's user may take it.
Add the taken reinforcement to the user's own hand; this does not grant retrieval of the user's own reinforcement discards.
Reserve Wild pickup is optional for each eligible discard. Declining one does not end the encounter-long effect or prevent taking a later eligible discard.
Vulch Super is not capped at one otherwise-eligible flare from a simultaneous discard group; its effect applies to all otherwise-eligible discarded flares.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Card information, discards and exhaustion
evidence.text: Hand size is public; card faces are private unless an effect says otherwise. You may make claims or lie about your hand during ordinary public table talk, but cannot show it; Mind has an additional secrecy restriction and deal terms must be honored. Table talk is public unless an effect permits secrecy. Discards are faceup and public, including all cards discarded together. When discard order matters, discard non-encounter cards first in alphabetical/numerical order, then encounter cards starting with offense clockwise and ending with defense, whose encounter card is on top.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Power loss, zapping and timing
evidence.text: Effects associated with no player resolve last, after the player order. Resolve actual simultaneous contradictory effects in order: **offense; defense; other players clockwise starting left of offense**. First honor more specific before/after timing within a phase. Finish one effect before starting another, except a Zap or an effect expressly allowing interruption. An optional effect's owner may change their mind when another effect or timing order changes the game state. Alien powers are normally usable once per relevant context, unless their text says otherwise.

evidence.heading: Reserve
evidence.quote:
#### Reserve

**Reinforce — Main player or ally only; optional; Reveal.**

- After encounter cards revealed may play one or more attack cards of 06 OR LESS from hand as reinforcement cards of listed value.

**FAQ pp5,19:** Choose all attacks for one use together. If the power is zapped, keep the card you were about to play. Reserve Wild need only be played once in the encounter.
